newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech M2 data point to no quick rate cut - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech M2 data point to no quick rate cut - analysts.

text.p: Slower growth in Czech money supply in January has given the central bank room to lower interest rates but most analysts said on Tuesday that no immediate cut was likely.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) said its key M2 money supply measure grew 8.4 percent year-on-year in January after 9.2 percent growth in December. The bank has set a target for M2 growth of 8-12 percent year-on-year for December 1997.
If the large deposits involved in the equity expansion of SPT Telecom were included, M2 rose 7.1 percent in January, compared with 7.8 percent in December.
"I do not see any reason for immediate (CNB) action or a strong response to this figure," said economist Martin Kupka of Patria Finance.

"This growth is approaching the bottom of the range the central bank would like M2 to grow this year but it is not out of the range and I think the central bank should not be very uncomfortable with that," he said.
"If M2 growth got below eight percent then the bank should think about relaxing its policies and allowing M2 to get closer to 10 percent," he said.

Kupka said he thought it unlikely the CNB would change rates at its regular board meeting this Thursday. He said he would wait until June to assess the impact on the economy of a package of measures introduced by the government last week to cut internal and external deficits and spur growth.

In announcing the package, the government also called for monetary policy to be less restrictive. But CNB vice-governor Jan Vit said on Tuesday inflation and stability in monetary policy were the central bank's key concerns
Peter Korous, head of corporate desk at CSOB, also believed a rate cut was not imminent.

"The consensus is that there will be a 50 basis point cut in the Lombard and discount rate and 20-30 in the repo rates but the question is the timing and the consensus is that it won't happen this Thursday," he said.

The Czech crown was little changed after the M2 figures, after rising half a percentage point earlier on better-than- expected trade figures for March, which showed a deficit of 13.4 billion crowns against analyst expectations of 17 billion.
Korous expected the crown to trade in a range of -0.8 percent to -1.45 percent against the central point of its mark/dollar basket.
At 1550 GMT, it stood at -1.30 percent.
But Lubos Kacmaric, bond trader at Creditanstalt in Prague, said a rate cut was possible this week.
"All the numbers that are coming out of the economy are showing big room to ease the policy," he said, adding that perceptions of a cut were already built into the crown's price.

"At this point, the only argument that the National Bank may use for not cutting rates this week is to wait for a certain time and pretend to be very independent of the government," he said, acknowledging the CNB liked to surprise the market.
